newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Research Alert - Reduce MIM stake - Wilson.
newsitem.headline: Research Alert - Reduce MIM stake - Wilson.

text.p: Brokerage firm Wilson HTM Ltd said it was recommending investors sell down their MIM Holdings Ltd shares following expectations the base metals giant would underperform over the next few months.
"A trading sell. MIM's recent share rally was premature and we expect it to underperform over the next few months," Wilson's director of resources research Phil Hutchings said in a report.
Hutchings also said the recent fall in gold prices would hurt the group's plans for the gold-rich Alumbrera mine in South America.
At a share price of A$1.80 at the time of the report, MIM was on a price-earnings of 33 times for 1998, Hutchings said.
MIM shares were three cents higher at A$1.77 at 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT). The stock has traded as high as A$2.10 in 1997 and as low as A$1.61.
Hutchings said MIM's earnings were still very weak with Wilson forecasting a modest net profit of A$6 million for the year ended June 30, 1997, rising to $88 million in 1997/98.
Both the Alumbrera project and the group's Ernest Henry copper-gold mine in Queensland were expected to begin production later this year but had quite extensive build-up periods.
"So their impact on earnings may not be felt for 12 to 18 months," Hutchings said.

About 40 percent of Alumbrera's revenue would come from gold production. "It is a relatively gold-rich mine compared with other major copper-gold porphyries. Alumbrera will initially produce more gold than (Papua New Guinea mine) Lihir," he said.

The recent fall in gold prices occurred before MIM could hedge a significant amount of gold and this meant the cash cost of copper production from Alumbrera would be higher than previously thought, Hutchings said.
"MIM is essentially rebuilding its entire asset base," he said.
"Subject to Alumbrera and Ernest Henry meeting expectations, we do believe that MIM shares should be great performers later in the decade," Hutchings said.
"But right now, it is too early," he said.
